               The      consonant             sounds         /m/,     /n/    and      /n/

               The  consonant  sounds /m/, /n/ and    are made  by stopping the flow of air out of the mouth so
               that it goes through the nose instead. The three sounds are different because the air is stopped b
               different parts of the mouth. You can feel this when you say the words  some, sun, sung.
          46a    Listen to the sound /m/. Look  at the mouth diagram  to see how  to make this sound.
         A     Note: Always close your lips for /m/, even at the end of a word when the next word begins with /k/ or
               /g/, for example: cream cake; warm glow.
